newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh opposition to end parliament boycott.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh opposition to end parliament boycott.

text.p: The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) agreed on Tuesday to return to parliament when it begins its winter session on Wednesday.
The decision came at a meeting of parliamentary experts of the BNP and the ruling Awami League chaired by Speaker Humayun Rasheed Choudhury.
Legislators of the BNP, headed by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, walked out of the last session of parliament in November.
They complained of the "repression and arrest of BNP leaders and workers in a motivated police crackdown, and refusal by the ruling party to voice their grievances in parliament."
They also said the speaker, an Awami League member, was not neutral.
"The allegations are not true," Hasina said earlier this week.
Choudhury said on Tuesday he would remain neutral in running parliament and try to ensure that opposition MPs get full exposure on state-run radio and television.
Government sources said the BNP and Awami League signed an agreement at Tuesday's meeting pledging to respect parliamentary norms, and this paved the way for BNP's return to parliament.
BNP lost to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League in general elections last June.

Hasina said on Friday that, "If the opposition remains absent from parliament for 90 consecutive working days, their seats will fall vacant and by-elections will have to be be called to fill them out."
